entities.summary:
Bjarni Herjólfsson, an Icelandic merchant mariner, holds the distinction of being the first known European to sight the mainland of the Americas, an accidental discovery occurring in 986 CE. His voyage, originating from Iceland and bound for the Norse settlements in Greenland, became a pivotal moment in the history of transatlantic exploration, directly preceding the more deliberate expeditions of Leif Erikson. Herjólfsson's journey underscores the expansive reach and navigational prowess of the Norse during the Viking Age, pushing the known boundaries of the European world westward into uncharted territories.

Herjólfsson's fateful journey began when his ship was blown off course by a storm while attempting to navigate from Eyrarbakki, Iceland, to the newly established Norse colonies in Greenland, recently founded by Erik the Red. After days of being adrift in dense fog, he and his crew sighted land that did not match the descriptions of Greenland: it was a flat, forested country, unlike the icy, mountainous terrain they expected. Despite his crew's pleas, Bjarni, steadfast in his original mission, refused to disembark and explore these new shores, instead turning his ship eastward. Over subsequent days, they sighted two more distinct landmasses—one appearing flat and wooded, the other mountainous with glaciers—before finally reaching Greenland, having sailed past three distinct regions of the North American coastline.
